display_policy.single_ppu_note: the whole battlefield is one 32 PPU grid: one 32x32 ground square per cell, a 32x8 front face for depth, structures and units on the same grid; every native pixel is exactly 6 screen pixels at the canonical tier, so nothing can drift out of scale against anything else
display_policy.non_integer_resolution_policy: integer scale plus letterbox; never fractional upscale and never half-pixel placement
display_policy.reference_basis: measured from the primary reference: one integer upscale of a native buffer, unlit areas keep zero intra-block variance and lighting is composited after the upscale

lighting_policy.scene_lighting: forbidden in the asset: no baked light pool, no cast floor shadow, no vignette, no ambient darkening gradient, no darkened border, no torch or aether glow
lighting_policy.form_shading: the only shading the asset carries: one fixed upper-left direction (lit top face, dark front face) so a solid reads as a volume; this is shape language, not illumination, and no role may vary it
lighting_policy.runtime_owner: URP 2D Light2D (day cycle, character light, baked shadow overlay sprites) owns all scene light and shadow at runtime
lighting_policy.reason: the reference measures zero intra-block variance in unlit regions and 5-10 percent changed pixels in lit regions, which is only possible when light is applied after the integer upscale rather than painted into the art
reject_if: floor shadow or light pool baked into a ground tile
global ambient gradient across the piece
torch or aether glow baked into a prop

scene_assembly_contract.wall_mount_rule: dedicated wall-mounted source and wall anchor required; do not raise a floor-standing prop
scene_assembly_contract.tabletop_rule: declare support asset and native support height
scene_assembly_contract.palette_rule: lock material_palette_family and upper-left form light before the first source in a scene batch; regenerate mismatched assets instead of recolouring them during assembly

generation_loop.source_policy: new independent Image output for every retry

shared_prompt.pixel_language: authentic coarse low-resolution pixel design shown enlarged with one uniform square macro-pixel lattice across the complete subject; large deliberate clusters; crisp hard edges; sparse controlled detail; limited cohesive palette; do not force the subject into a 32x32 generated-image composition
shared_prompt.ground_square: the subject is exactly one square battlefield cell, complete and self-contained: a near-flat paving square with at most three darker clusters and a clearly visible 1-pixel border on all four edges in the material's own dark tone (never pure black), plus a slightly lighter lip just inside that border; the whole design spans about 32 macro pixels across, not a crop of a larger floor
shared_prompt.illumination: flat even illumination with no directional scene light, no cast shadows, no glow and no darkening at the edges; the only shading is the fixed upper-left form shading on solid volumes
shared_prompt.reference_policy: Sephiria screenshot controls map readability and density; an approved OCC asset controls family scale (for paving: ArtSource/sephiria_style_study_2026-09-16/project_assets/approved_ground_stone_16_at6x.png - 2 colours, dominant 88 percent, zero isolated pixels); references never authorize copying their subject design
shared_prompt.avoid: antialiasing, blur, gradients, tiny decoration, high-frequency texture, isolated speckles, high-resolution illustration compressed to appear pixelated, baked lighting or shadow, evenly spread palette steps that read as dither noise

ground_field_32.view: orthographic top-down material field: exactly one square gameplay cell, self-contained; no object, no facade, no neighbouring tile
ground_field_32.target_palette: 3 or fewer: the approved stone baseline uses 2
ground_field_32.baked_cell_border: required: 1 native px on all four edges in the material's own dark tone (never pure black), plus a 1 px lighter lip inside it so the square reads as raised; adjacent tiles must overlap into one seam line
ground_field_32.why_border: this version ships no material transitions, so the baked border is the only visible cell separation and it also gives the map editor an obvious square to select
ground_field_32.surface_detail_policy: near-flat field: dominant tone at least 45 percent and for a paving theme target 75-90 percent; at most three connected darker clusters; isolated one pixel noise forbidden; no dithering, no gradient, no microtexture
ground_field_32.lighting: no scene lighting; a paving surface stays tonally neutral (no directional shading); see lighting_policy
reject_if: even spread of all palette steps (dither noise)
a fragment of a larger design rather than one whole square

ground_front_face_32x8.view: the south front face of one raised ground square: a 32x8 strip showing the tile's thickness
ground_front_face_32x8.placement: bottom edge of the owning cell, overlapping the top 8 px of the next row; drawn after the next row's ground and before that row's walls, structures, props and units; optional per cell, added where a height step is wanted
ground_front_face_32x8.surface_detail_policy: one flat face tone plus at most two connected darker bands; dominant tone at least 45 percent; the topmost 1 px repeats the tile border tone so the face joins the border without a seam
ground_front_face_32x8.lighting: no scene lighting; the face is darker than the tile top by material form only; see lighting_policy
reject_if: lighting or cast shadow baked in
face tone lighter than the tile top

permanent_wall_32x32.view: orthographic top-down pseudo-2.5D: one solid pillar block filling its whole gameplay cell, with a square top surface and a front face turned toward the bottom of the screen, the left and right sides slightly inset so it reads as a standing column
permanent_wall_32x32.canvas: fixed_32x32, fully opaque, filling the cell edge to edge, no overhang in any direction
permanent_wall_32x32.reading: a stage-appropriate solid wall block whose material follows the current region; in the academy stage it should read as clear Japanese-fantasy magical-academy architecture with a legible top and darker front face, while remaining solid and thick enough to read as indestructible terrain
permanent_wall_32x32.tiling: all four edges are edge-to-edge and match, so four identical blocks tile with no gap and no seam; a run of them reads as a continuous wall
permanent_wall_32x32.lighting: no scene lighting; fixed upper-left form shading only; see lighting_policy
reject_if: baked scene lighting or floor shadow
a low wall strip that does not fill the cell

directional_edge_32x40.view: one 32x32 walkable surface aligned to the board edge plus an 8 px exterior facade hanging outside the board
directional_edge_32x40.rotation_policy: authored per direction; runtime rotation forbidden when the piece carries light, facade, wear or shadow direction

unit_sideview.view: strict 90-degree side profile; only one eye may be visible; torso, pelvis, feet and equipment all face the same side
unit_sideview.visual_footprint_note: the canvas may exceed one gameplay cell: OCC characters are deliberately about two cells tall while the reference is about 1.2
unit_sideview.height_range_note: user decision 2026-09-16: the fire mage (body 51 px = 1.59 of a 32 px cell) is the approved proportion; a new humanoid should read as clearly overhanging its cell, so aim at 46-58 px. Quadrupeds and genuinely small units are judged separately and may sit inside their cell.

prop_oblique.view: shared oblique top-down map view with visible top and front faces; screen-axis alignment; never diagonal placement

deterministic_postprocess: never_paint_or_restore_lighting: a source whose lighting was removed by decoding is rejected, not repaired

reject_when_the_decoded_design_field_exceeds_1_4x_the_delivery_in_either_axis: a window that crops a finer-grained design yields a fragment of a bigger picture rather than one whole square, which is the recorded failure mode for ground tiles

importer.atlas: padding 0, rotation off, tight packing off, extrude 0
importer.reason: a tight mesh crops the quad and shifts the sprite off the native pixel lattice, which breaks both uniform pixel size and seam-free adjacency

runtime_lattice_check.method: capture the running game at the target resolution and measure block uniformity: the true tier makes nearly every p x p block internally uniform at p = screen px per native px, and the lattice must be aligned to the image origin
runtime_lattice_check.pass_condition: integer tier detected at the expected canonical multiple, lattice offset zero on both axes

placement_rules: R1 gameplay cell = 32x32 native px; exactly one 32x32 ground tile per cell, no subgrid and no cross-cell base texture
R2 objects anchor bottom-center to the owning cell bottom edge; multi-cell objects own their bottom-left cell

R3 overhang above, left and right is allowed; overhang past the footprint bottom edge toward the screen bottom is forbidden, except for the ground front face which is defined to overhang its own cell southward by 8 px
R4 layer order back to front: ground, ground front faces, ground overlays, walls, large structures, small props, units, overlays
R5 within a layer sort by bottom-edge y ascending, then structure < prop < unit
R6 units keep a 32x64 canvas with the body on the canvas bottom edge and a zero foot offset
R7 a ground front face is drawn after the next row's ground and before any wall, structure, prop or unit in that row
R8 new assets declare application scope, mount type, native anchor, visible contact line, depth baseline and support before generation
R9 floor-standing, wall-mounted and tabletop variants are separate roles; scene coordinates cannot change mount type
R10 runtime rooms split walkable ground, blocking walls, directional edges or front faces and independent props; combined shells are concept-only
R11 verify walkability, collision, click ownership and occlusion before aesthetic approval
R12 record native coordinates and draw order and review the assembly at 1x and canonical 6x
runtime_promotion_gates.formal_requires: machine PASS plus human PASS plus stable GUID plus verified importer plus a runtime contact capture that passes the lattice check

stability_baseline_2026_09_14.interpretation: one-shot generation is not stable enough for unattended promotion; automatic rejection plus one targeted regeneration is part of the production loop
